# Today on Hacker News

## AI/ML
The Mistral AI Now Summit has captured attention with insights on the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. Notable discussions included key takeaways from the summit, where significant developments and future directions in AI were shared. For further reading, see the post titled [Notes from the Mistral AI Now Summit](https://koenvangilst.nl/lab/mistral-ai-now-summit).

## Programming
Programming enthusiasts have been buzzing about the new features in Zig's build system, detailed in the post [Zig: Build System Reworked](https://ziglang.org/devlog/2026/#2026-05-26). Additionally, the release of Openrsync by the OpenBSD team offers a fresh implementation of the popular rsync tool, which can be found in the post [Openrsync: An implementation of rsync, by the OpenBSD team](https://github.com/kristapsdz/openrsync). 

## Science/Technology
A significant shift in funding policies has been proposed with new US rules that allow the cancellation of grants at any time. This has sparked discussions on its implications for scientific research, as seen in the post [Proposed new US funding rules: We can cancel any grant at any time](https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/05/the-office-of-management-and-budget-tries-again-to-cripple-us-science/). In consumer technology, IXI's autofocusing lenses are nearing readiness, potentially replacing multifocal glasses, as highlighted in the article [IXI's autofocusing lenses are almost ready to replace multifocal glasses](https://www.engadget.com/wearables/ixis-autofocusing-lenses-multifocal-glasses-ces-2026-212608427.html).

## Miscellaneous
In a notable governance move, a Danish pension fund has excluded SpaceX from its investments, raising eyebrows and questions about corporate governance in the space industry, discussed in the article [Danish pension fund excludes SpaceX citing governance and valuation](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/danish-pension-fund-excludes-spacex-citing-governance-valuation-2026-05-29/). Another interesting story discusses the evolution of print technology with the release of open-source ColorMix for PrusaSlicer, allowing users to print with dozens of colors, as seen in [Print with dozens of colors: Our new open-source ColorMix for PrusaSlicer](https://blog.prusa3d.com/our-new-open-source-colormix-model-in-prusaslicer-and-easyprint_136079/). 

Overall, today's discussions on Hacker News reflect a diverse range of interests, from advancements in AI to significant shifts in funding and technology in everyday life.
